Folder Review's own source is licensed under MIT. Dependencies retain their licenses.

Runtime: CPython 3.13.16 (PSF and bundled component notices), Tcl/Tk,
XlsxWriter (BSD-2-Clause), BLAKE3 (CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0), olefile (BSD),
rarfile (ISC), Brotli (MIT), texttable (MIT), psutil (BSD-3-Clause),
backports.zstd (PSF-2.0 and zstd notices), pycryptodomex (BSD/Public Domain),
py7zr, multivolumefile, inflate64, pybcj and pyppmd (LGPL-2.1-or-later).
Actual versions and verified native origins are listed in components.json.
openpyxl/et-xmlfile are test readers only and are not bundled in the EXE.

This distribution includes unmodified 7-Zip 26.04 7z.exe and 7z.dll,
under GNU LGPL with BSD-licensed code and the unRAR restriction.
See 7zip-license.txt, third-party-licenses/, and https://www.7-zip.org/.
Complete corresponding sources for 7-Zip and the LGPL Python libraries
are supplied in third-party-sources.zip with verified upstream hashes.

Users may modify/rebuild the separately licensed components and debug their
modifications under their licenses. Project MIT terms impose no additional
restriction on reverse engineering, modification, or replacement of LGPL parts.
Python's notices retain Microsoft's conditions for its Windows runtime code.

PyInstaller's bootloader is GPL with a distribution exception allowing bundled
applications to retain their own licenses. Its license text is included.
All license texts are in the full package and embedded in the standalone EXE.
Run folder-review.exe --licenses to print them without network access.
